title: Exact and asymptotic CPU verification solutions
units: Equations use SI unless the symbol explicitly states otherwise. SimRep converts to mm, us, V, gauss, amu, elementary charges, and eV. A kinetic energy per charge in joules/coulomb is a voltage; for singly charged ions its numerical value equals the energy in eV.
method: Each case names executable public Rust CPU API tests, not a second implementation of SimRep. Formula provenance is explicitly derived here: no unchecked textbook page or equation is claimed. Spatial or temporal three-level Celik GCI uses a safety factor of 1.25 where the observable has identifiable monotone convergence. Roundoff-limited or finite-ray cases remain OPEN without an invented uncertainty. Test tolerances and approximation envelopes are not numerical uncertainties. MISS is reported, not hidden by widening a tolerance.

model.adaptation: A formula inventory connected to executable verification cases and computed verdicts. All formulas and implementation links below are independently specified for ion optics.

omitted.reason: No universal closed focal-length formula exists without an axial potential profile and an approximation regime. A field-profile integral or numerical ray matrix is not an exact solution specified by electrode voltage and dimensions alone; omitted rather than inventing a closed form.

U.meaning: signed voltage producing positive transverse field

d,L,y,y_0.meaning: plate gap, active length, transverse position and launch position

v_x,v_{y0}.meaning: constant longitudinal and initial transverse velocities

q,m,t.meaning: particle charge, mass and flight time

cases.validity: Infinite plates, uniform static field with no fringe field; nonrelativistic; no space charge or collisions; trajectory remains within the gap.

derivation: Newton-Lorentz gives x''=0 and y''=qU/(md).
Integrate twice with the launch position and velocity.
Set x-x0=L=v_x t and substitute t=L/v_x.

cases.tolerance: 1e-10 mm absolute deflection; 1e-12 us transit time; uniform polynomial trajectory, u_num not identifiable.

q,m,U,d.meaning: charge, mass, voltage and plate gap

L,v_0,t.meaning: flight distance, initial longitudinal speed and elapsed TOF

cases.validity: Same idealizations as parallel-plate deflection; positive physical root with detector reachable. Existing test launches from rest and also verifies that birth time is excluded from TOF.

derivation: Integrate x''=a to L=v0 t+a t^2/2.
Take the positive quadratic root and rationalize it.
For v0=0 obtain sqrt(2L/a); absolute arrival time is birth time plus t.

cases.tolerance: Existing relative TOF tolerance 1e-12; reused, not duplicated; roundoff-limited OPEN gate.

cases.physics: Concentric spherical electrostatic analyzer pass energy and 180-degree first-order focusing

R_1,R_2,R_0,r,delta r.meaning: inner, outer, mean, trajectory radius and radial perturbation

K_0,q.meaning: central kinetic energy and positive ion charge

theta,theta_f,alpha.meaning: bend angle, first-order focus angle and small launch-angle error

cases.validity: Nonrelativistic positive ions, attractive inverse-square electric force, ideal concentric spherical surfaces with no fringes. Stated rational passband assumes arithmetic mean orbit radius, not an arbitrary radius. The focus is first-order angular focusing, not zero finite-angle aberration or a claim of finite aperture energy bandwidth.

derivation: Spherical Laplace gives Phi=A-B/r; impose Phi(R2)-Phi(R1)=U to obtain B.
The circular-orbit equation m v^2/R0=qB/R0^2 gives K0/q=B/(2R0).
For radial force proportional to r^(-s), linearize the Binet equation in u=1/r: delta u''+(3-s)delta u=0.
Here s=2, so a launch-angle perturbation is proportional to sin(theta); its first angular focus is pi.

cases.tolerance: Central exit radius relative tolerance 5e-5 with 128/256/512-step GCI; normalized odd angular response below 2e-5 per rad at alpha=1e-3 rad and 4096 steps, no uncertainty assigned to paraxial limit.

cases.physics: Coaxial cylindrical analyzer pass energy and 127.279-degree first-order radial focusing

Phi,A,U.meaning: potential, inner gauge and outer-minus-inner voltage

R_1,R_2,R_0,r,delta r.meaning: electrode, reference, trajectory radii and perturbation

K_0,q.meaning: central kinetic energy and positive charge

alpha,theta,theta_f.meaning: small launch-angle error, bend angle and radial focus

cases.validity: Infinite coaxial cylinders; nonrelativistic positive ions; no end/fringe field; first-order radial focusing only. An ideal cylindrical analyzer has no analogous axial focusing.

derivation: Integrate cylindrical Laplace (r Phi')'=0 with voltage difference U.
Balance m v^2/r=qU/[r ln(R2/R1)] to find the radius-independent pass energy.
Linearize Binet as in the spherical case, now s=1; delta u''+2 delta u=0.
The first zero after launch is theta=pi/sqrt(2), commonly rounded to 127 degrees.

cases.tolerance: Same central-ray and angular-response bands as spherical analyzer; this is a pass-energy check, not a finite-aperture spectral bandwidth. Circular-ray step differences below 64 binary64 eps times the observable scale are roundoff-limited; no spurious GCI is assigned.

cases.physics: Asymptotic voltage-to-pass-energy calibration for toroidal surfaces

E_n,U.meaning: gap-normal electric field and electrode voltage difference

d,R_0,a.meaning: full gap, equatorial reference orbit radius and poloidal curvature radius

K_0,q,k.meaning: pass energy, charge and explicitly defined calibration constant

cases.validity: Asymptotic, not an exact finite-gap torus solution: d/R0 and d/a must be small; symmetric gap about reference surface, no fringes. The convention k=U/(K/q) matters; some analyzer literature uses its reciprocal. Test uses circular torus minor radii 0.9 and 1.1 mm, major radius 4 mm, R0=5 mm, d=0.2 mm.

derivation: In normal coordinates across a smooth thin gap, the leading Laplace operator is d^2/dn^2, hence Phi is linear to leading order and En~U/d.
Equatorial circular-orbit balance gives 2K0/R0=q En.
Define k=U/(K0/q) and substitute En. Curvature corrections remain at finite gap and are not numerical uncertainty.

cases.tolerance: 2% relative approximation envelope; independent axisymmetric cut-cell Laplace solves on 49/97/193 grids; GCI estimates discretization only. A MISS against the leading asymptote is a finite-gap finding, not by itself a solver defect.

formulas_latex: \omega_c=|q|B/(\gamma m),\quad r_c=p_\perp/(|q|B)=\gamma m v_\perp/(|q|B),\quad T_c=2\pi\gamma m/(|q|B)

v,v_perp,c.meaning: total and perpendicular speed and speed of light

K,m,q,B,p_perp.unit: J, kg, C, T, kg m/s
K,m,q,B,p_perp.meaning: kinetic energy, rest mass, charge, field and transverse momentum

omega_c,r_c,T_c.meaning: cyclotron angular frequency, radius and period

cases.validity: Uniform static B, no E, collisions, radiation reaction or collective effects; test has perpendicular launch and K=1 GeV for mass 1 amu. Gamma is constant because magnetic force does no work.

derivation: Start with d(gamma m v)/dt=q v cross B.
Dot with v: kinetic energy and gamma are constant.
The perpendicular velocity rotates at |q|B/(gamma m); integrate its rotation to obtain radius and period.
The test infers the period from the quarter-orbit position angle, not by substituting the requested duration as a measured period.

cases.tolerance: Relative radius and inferred-period tolerances 2e-6; relativistic Boris 128/256/512 steps per quarter orbit; three-step GCI. Existing nonrelativistic 1000-orbit energy test is not duplicated.

omega_c,t,x,y.meaning: signed nonrelativistic frequency qB/m, time and positions

cases.validity: Nonrelativistic uniform perpendicular fields; the displayed trajectory starts at rest at the origin. Drift is independent of mass and charge, but gyromotion is not. SimRep conversion is vD[mm/us]=1e4 (E[V/mm] cross B[G])/|B[G]|^2.

derivation: Write v=vD+w and choose E+vD cross B=0.
The remaining equation is pure gyromotion for w.
Integrate the rest-launch initial condition; after one physical gyroperiod the sine/cosine terms cancel and displacement/T equals vD.

cases.tolerance: Mean drift relative tolerance 2e-5; 128/256/512 Boris steps per physical gyroperiod with temporal GCI.

cases.physics: Crossed electric/magnetic force cancellation and velocity selection

E,B,v_perp.meaning: orthogonal electric and magnetic fields and selected transverse speed

cases.validity: Uniform perpendicular fields; direction must satisfy the vector equation, not just the speed ratio. Any parallel-to-B velocity is unconstrained. Force cancellation is also relativistically valid, but this test is nonrelativistic.

derivation: Set the Lorentz force q(E+v cross B) to zero.
For perpendicular fields choose v=(E cross B)/B^2, obtaining selected speed E/B.
The test also detunes the incident speed by 10% and checks the analytic transverse displacement, so a field implementation returning zero cannot pass.

cases.tolerance: Selected-ray transverse displacement and longitudinal position below 1e-12 mm absolute; detuned-ray displacement relative tolerance 1e-5; balanced solution is roundoff-limited OPEN.

cases.physics: Potential between infinite coaxial cylindrical conductors
cases.validity: R1<r<R2, infinite coaxial cylinders, vacuum, no volume charge. Existing Cartesian cut-cell test uses four grid phases and exact conductor surfaces; no staircase-boundary substitution.

derivation: Cylindrical symmetry reduces Laplace to (r Phi')'=0.
Integrate to Phi=A+B ln r and impose both conductor voltages.
Differentiate with E=-grad Phi for the field.

cases.tolerance: Reuse 17/33/65 grids and worst of four phases; existing max potential error <6h^2 V and near-surface field error <20h V/mm; GCI of maximum potential-error norm. Order gates remain OPEN.

cases.validity: R1<r<R2, concentric spherical conductors, vacuum, no volume charge; exact surfaces and four grid phases in the existing 3D solver test.

derivation: Spherical symmetry reduces Laplace to (r^2 Phi')'=0.
Integrate to Phi=A+B/r, apply the two Dirichlet voltages.
Differentiate to obtain the inverse-square radial field.

cases.tolerance: Same existing grids, phase sweep and absolute envelopes as coaxial case; GCI of maximum potential-error norm; any pre-asymptotic order miss remains a finding.

formulas_latex: \Phi(\mathbf r)=\frac{Q}{4\pi\epsilon_0 r},\quad \mathbf E(\mathbf r)=\frac{Q\mathbf r}{4\pi\epsilon_0 r^3}
cases.validity: Vacuum point charge at nonzero separation; no softening, self-force or conductor images. Existing test checks the DirectCharge field, not a potential-output API, and also checks represented-charge weights and equal/opposite fields.

derivation: Gauss's law on a sphere gives 4 pi r^2 Er=Q/epsilon0.
Choose Phi(infinity)=0 and integrate -Er to obtain the potential.
Use the displacement direction to write the vector field.

cases.tolerance: Reuse existing absolute field tolerance 1e-16 V/mm at 2 mm separation for Q=1e-15 C; direct algebra has no identifiable grid uncertainty.

cases.physics: Cold symmetric repulsive two-body Coulomb expansion

q,Q,m.meaning: test charge, other represented source charge and particle mass

cases.validity: Equal particle masses, equal positive represented source charges, symmetric rest launch, unsoftened vacuum Coulomb interaction, no external fields. The source charge Q may represent a macro-particle; q/m remains the physical particle charge-to-mass ratio.

derivation: At separation 2R the force on either particle is qQ/[4 pi epsilon0 (2R)^2], hence R''=C/R^2.
Multiply by R' and integrate: R'^2=2C(1/Ri-1/R).
Separate variables with s=R/Ri and integrate sqrt(s/(s-1)); the primitive is sqrt(s(s-1))+asinh(sqrt(s-1)).
The existing test bisects this monotone implicit time relation and compares the coupled ensemble trajectory.

cases.tolerance: Reuse dt=0.04/0.02/0.01 us at t=0.7 us with Ri=1 mm and total represented charge 2e-14 C; adjacent error ratios >3.7, symmetry exact; three-step GCI on final half-separation.

epsilon_0,e,m.meaning: vacuum permittivity, positive elementary charge and electron mass

V_A,V.meaning: anode voltage and potential relative to cathode

x,d,v,rho.meaning: distance from cathode, full gap, electron speed and negative charge density

cases.validity: One-dimensional infinite plates, steady mono-species collisionless nonrelativistic electrons, zero cathode injection speed and field, no magnetic field. Density is singular at x=0. The SimRep test supplies this analytical density on x/d in [1/8,1] and verifies Poisson/current consistency; it does not claim that a self-consistent emission boundary or limiting-current search is implemented.

derivation: Energy conservation gives m v^2/2=e V and continuity gives rho=-J/v.
Poisson becomes V''=(J/epsilon0) sqrt(m/(2e)) V^(-1/2).
Multiply by V' and integrate with V(0)=V'(0)=0: V'^2=4(J/epsilon0)sqrt(m/(2e))sqrt(V).
Integrate again and impose V(d)=VA to obtain V=VA(x/d)^(4/3) and the 4/9 current prefactor.
Test uses d=1 mm and VA=50 V, converts speed from mm/us to mm/s, and reconstructs J=epsilon0 V'' sqrt(2eV/m) from the solved profile at x/d=9/16.

cases.tolerance: Relative reconstructed-current tolerance 2e-4; 17/33/65-point axial grids and three-grid GCI. SI current density is converted to A/mm^2 for gate output.
